# The scribl story

This is the narrative spine of the project brain: how scribl went from a client
brief to a running proof of concept, and where the work goes next. scribl is a
consumer daily-creative mobile-app POC (Expo / React Native with a thin
serverless AWS backend), built as a reference proof of an AI-assisted SDLC. Read
this end to end for the plot; follow the links for the detail.

## From wireframes to detail (discovery and design)

The engagement started with the client's own materials: a business brief and
MVP scope, and a PRFAQ that framed the product vision and the "why now." Those
verbatim source artifacts are curated in [Input Artifacts](/input-artifacts).

The requirements are captured in the [MVP scope / BRD](/context/documents/scribl-d2c-mvp-scope)
and the [D2C MLP PRFAQ](/context/documents/scribl-d2c-mlp-prfaq). The first shape
of the product came through as a [D2C user-flow wireframe](/context/media/scribl-d2c-flow),
then as visual design: an [early full-app UI mockup](/assets/context/scribl-d2c-ui-mockup.html)
gave the early direction, and the [latest designs](/context/design-history/latest-designs)
carry the current look across the hero screens. Together these set what the app
should feel like before a line of build code existed.

## Researching the implementation (research and architecture)

With the intent understood, the work turned to how to build it. The research
notes distill the engagement: the [client summary](/knowledge/research/scribl-client-summary),
the [engagement approach](/knowledge/research/scribl-engagement-approach), the
[technical implementation plan](/knowledge/research/scribl-technical-implementation-plan),
the [team model](/knowledge/research/scribl-team-model), and the
[POC AWS architecture](/knowledge/research/scribl-poc-aws-architecture). The
[approach-discussion meeting](/knowledge/meetings/scribl-approach-discussion)
records the conversation that aligned everyone on that direction.

The production target was drawn as an [AWS architecture diagram](/context/media/scribl-aws-architecture-d2c)
and priced in the [cost model](/context/pages/reference/poc/architecture/cost-model).
The load-bearing technical choices are ratified as ADRs: see the
[decision record index](/context/pages/reference/decisions/README) for React
Native as primary, serverless-first backend, DynamoDB single-table, the Claude
provider abstraction, model tiering, and the rest.

## Building the POC (build)

The build contract is the [full-app spec](/scribl-full-app-spec): the single
authoritative description of what the app does end to end, what "done" means,
and which decisions are still open. It is what the implementation "bake-out"
builds against. Where the app stands right now lives in [Status](/status), and
the working conventions -- definition of ready, definition of done, and team
process -- are in the [Handbook](/handbook/).

## Roadmap and delivery

The plan from intake to a demo-able POC is the [Roadmap](/roadmap), tracked in
phases and milestones. Day-to-day work moves across the [Board](/board) (Now /
Next / Blocked / Done), and each work item has its own card under
[Stories](/stories/) with acceptance criteria checked off as code ships.

## Toward production

The POC is a thin slice of the production target, not a throwaway. What it takes
to go past the POC -- the seams the POC is shaped toward but does not implement --
is captured in the [Production Starter Backlog](/production-backlog).
